background.summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who knows asymptotic notation, basic discrete mathematics, linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers, elementary algebra (groups, rings, modular arithmetic, polynomials), elementary number theory (primes, CRT) and basic probability/combinatorics. They know basic Turing machines and tapes and the schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, and probably the FFT as an algorithm. They have not studied multitape-machine algorithm engineering, Schönhage–Strassen or later multiplication algorithms, or specialist linear-algebra constructions such as Bruhat factorizations.
